the molecular evolution of GLP1R is driven by two rounds of genome duplication (2R) and local gene duplication, which is followed by the acquisition of specific changes in the amino-acid sequence.

The main takeaway from our work is that

gene duplication is an important mechanism for the evolution of peptide and receptor families and that specific changes in amino acid sequence after gene duplication contribute to the establishment of distinct yet related peptide-receptor pairs.
